scenes.title: Examiner's Margin — household expenditure
scenes.narration: Welcome to IELTS Winners. This household expenditure table compares Canada, Japan, Mexico and Germany across housing, food, transport and others. You'll learn to spot comparisons, write an overview without figures, and build a four-paragraph Task One answer.

scenes.title: Step 1 — Analyse the table with ERCS
scenes.narration: Step one: analyse the table with E R C S. Extremes: Others reaches forty-eight percent in Japan, while transport falls to ten percent. Rankings: Canada leads housing at twenty-eight percent; Mexico leads food at twenty-four. Comparisons: Others dominates in three countries. Spread: transport varies least, from ten to fourteen percent, while Others varies most.

scenes.title: Step 2 — The four-paragraph response
scenes.narration: Step two: use four paragraphs. Introduction: paraphrase the table. Overview: housing leads in Canada, while Others dominates elsewhere. Body one: compare housing and food, including Canada's twenty-eight percent and Mexico's twenty-four percent. Body two: compare transport and Others. Transport ranges from ten to fourteen percent; Others reaches forty-eight percent in Japan but fourteen in Canada. Group the figures logically.

scenes.title: Step 3 — Language toolkit
scenes.narration: Step three: use precise language. Forty-eight percent is nearly half; twenty-eight percent is slightly over a quarter; twenty-four percent is almost a quarter; twenty percent is one fifth; ten percent is one tenth. Useful expressions include accounted for, represented, and made up. Use whereas or in contrast for differences, and similarly for shared patterns. Keep figures out of the overview.

scenes.title: Steps 4 to 7 — Grouping and strategy
scenes.narration: Steps four to seven complete your strategy. Group housing with food and transport with Others. Upgrade basic descriptions: housing accounted for Canada's largest share, at twenty-eight percent. Avoid listing every figure, repeating the introduction in the overview, or comparing without supporting data. Finish with an introduction, overview and two clearly grouped body paragraphs.
